First attempted fix (commit ac94e81) simply removed the eligibility_status check and showed response.results directly -- this was WRONG: it broke an intentional CI safety guard (scripts/validate_nursing_ai_owned_ui.cjs, which asserts 'Only verified-eligible facilities may be presented as leading recommendations') and a Playwright E2E contract (a POTENTIALLY_ELIGIBLE facility must never render the 'Meets verified must-haves' confidence badge). Reverted, then fixed properly by resolving the root cause (nursing-gold-0001's fix) instead of bypassing the display gate.
dispute_notes: This case is itself a worked example of the 'don't discard disagreement' principle: the CI check disagreeing with my first fix was the signal that the fix was wrong, not the check.

reasoning_summary: Initial read was wrong in one respect: this was not a missing data-ingestion pipeline. The canonical registry already carries real CMS Five-Star fields for every skilled-nursing facility (cms_ccn, cms_overall_rating, cms_health_inspection_rating, cms_staffing_rating, cms_quality_measure_rating, cms_processing_date) -- confirmed by cross-checking Silver Ridge Healthcare Center's registry values (overall=4, inspection=3, staffing=2, qm=5) directly against CMS's own public Provider Data Catalog API (data.cms.gov/provider-data/api/1/datastore/query/4pq5-n9py/0, filtered by CCN 295072): identical. GET /canonical-facilities/{id}/regulatory-history simply never read those fields -- it only ever checked the Nevada HCQC/ALiS index. Fixed by adding a CMS-shaped fallback (rating_system: CMS_FIVE_STAR, kept separate from Nevada's A-D grade shape rather than force-mapped into it, since the two rating systems are not equivalent) that the endpoint uses when the Nevada index has nothing for a facility. Verified against 3 skilled-nursing facilities and confirmed the Nevada AGC path (Atria Seville) is unaffected.
dispute_notes: Superseded: originally flagged as a data-ingestion decision needing product sign-off. Turned out to be a straightforward surfacing bug once the registry was actually inspected -- the data was already there.

reasoning_summary: Correcting an earlier misdirected investigation of database/nevada_facility_universe_canonical.json: canonical_universe.py explicitly calls that file 'the stale Nevada repo artifact' and states production never falls back to it. The real production data source is the pinned, checksummed database/las_vegas_runtime_v3 blob (364 Valley records, last regenerated 2026-08-18, no automated refresh found in render.yaml or either active Render cron job). As of 2026-08-31, none of its 364 records has an expiration_date already in the past -- this is not an active incorrect recommendation today. But expiration_date is real, specific, per-facility data that the system already has and simply never uses: nothing compares it to the current date at request time, so a facility whose license lapses (or is suspended/revoked before its stated expiration) would be recommended identically to one in good standing, with no live signal to catch it. This is the 'facility record stale' category the gold schema anticipated, refined from a systemic data-freshness worry into a concrete, unused field with a knowable, currently-empty blast radius.
dispute_notes: Open product/infrastructure decision, not something to resolve unilaterally in code: (a) add a deterministic check comparing expiration_date to the current date at request time (cheap, no new data needed -- the field already exists in the pinned blob), (b) also build a scheduled job that reruns the Nevada HCQC scrape-and-finalize pipeline to catch early suspension/revocation that expiration_date alone can't (external-site scraping cadence, rate-limit and terms-of-service considerations, new Render cron service), or (c) explicitly accept the current risk (empirically zero facilities affected today) and revisit later. No fix commit -- this case documents a verified investigation finding, not a resolved bug.
